svg.title: Initial Θ-data, built four times — [IUTchI] Def 3.1

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Initial Θ-data, built four times: what it needs, how to make it, and the numbers

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Everything in inter-universal Teichmüller theory starts from one tuple (F̄/F, X_F, l, C̲_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε̲), fixed in [IUTchI] Def 3.1: a number field F, a once-punctured elliptic curve X_F over it, a prime l, a curve C̲_K over K = F(E[l]) that remembers

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: one line of l-torsion, a choice V of one place of K over each place of the field of moduli, the odd places of bad multiplicative reduction V^bad_mod, and a cusp ε̲. The left column is the recipe: for each step, the clause of Def 3.1 it has to meet and

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: how to meet it (F is chosen as in [IUTchIV] Thm 1.10). The four columns run the recipe on four elliptic curves over Q, three from abc triples and one given by its equation. Every number is computed exactly from the integers of the input, the SL2

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: condition is proved from point counts, and the abc examples are re-checked by the toolkit's own validator. All of it is saved as JSON, one file per example.

svg.text: Pick the elliptic curve: X_F and F_mod

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: X_F is a once-punctured elliptic curve (type (1,1)) over F, X_F ⊆ E_F; C_F = X_F/±1; F_mod ⊆ F is the field of moduli

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: Start from any E over Q; an abc triple a + b = c gives the Frey curve y² = x(x − a)(x + b). Compute b2, b4, b6, b8,

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: c4, c6, Δ and j = c4³/Δ exactly and check 1728Δ = c4³ − c6². Here j ∈ Q, so F_mod = Q(j) = Q.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Find the bad places and their q-parameters: V^bad_mod

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: V^bad_mod ⊆ V_mod is a non-empty set of non-archimedean places of odd residue characteristic at which X_F has

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: Over F the reduction is stable, so E is bad exactly where j is not integral: ord_p(j) < 0. There the Tate parameter has

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: ord_p(q_p) = −ord_p(j). Its p-adic digits come from inverting j = 1/q + 744 + 196884q + …, i.e. q = x + 744x² +

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: 750420x³ + … with x = 1/j. Keep the odd p. The place 2 can be bad, but it is never in V^bad_mod. The bars show

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: ord(q_v)·log p, the share of v in log q, on one scale for all four.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Build F̄/F, and the field K

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: √−1 ∈ F; F/F_mod Galois of degree prime to l; the 2·3-torsion of E_F rational over F; stable reduction at every finite

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: place. K = the field cut out by E[l].

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: Take F = F_mod(√−1, E[2·3·5]) and F̄ = Q̄. Gal(F/F_tpd) embeds in {±1} × GL2(F_3) × GL2(F_5) (order 2·48·480), so

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: [F:Q] divides [F_tpd:Q]·46080 and has no prime factor ≥ 7. Since E[3], E[5] ⊆ E(F), Raynaud's criterion gives

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: semistable reduction everywhere. Then K = F(E[l]). Bars are on a log scale, and ≤ marks a bound.

Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: l ≥ 5 prime, prime to the residue characteristics of V^bad_mod and to the orders ord(q_v) at V^bad, and the image

Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: Sieve 5, 7, 11, …: 5 always fails here because F already contains E[5]; strike any l in V^bad_mod or dividing some

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: ord(q_v); the first survivor whose SL2 condition is proved (step 5) is l. Then l* = (l − 1)/2 and l± = (l + 1)/2.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Prove that the image of Galois contains SL2(F_l)

svg.text: Frob_p (p ∤ lΔ) acts on E[l] with trace a_p = p + 1 − #E(F_p) and det p. By Serre (1972, §2.8 Prop 19) the image

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: contains SL2(F_l) once it has s: tr ≠ 0 and tr² − 4det a non-zero square; s′: tr ≠ 0 and tr² − 4det a non-square; s″: u =

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: tr²/det ∉ {0, 1, 2, 4} and u² − 3u + 1 ≠ 0. These rule out the Borel, the Cartan normalizers and A4, S4, A5. Over F

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: the image has index dividing [F:Q], which is prime to l, so it still contains SL2.

Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: C̲_K of type (1, l-tors)± over K with K-core C_F; V ⊆ V(K) one place over each place of F_mod, of type (1, Z/lZ)± at

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: V^bad; ε̲ a cusp from a non-zero element of Q.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Inter Display', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', Arial, sans-serif
'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: Pick a line in E[l] ≅ F_l². There are l + 1 lines, all K-rational. The quotient E[l] ↠ Q ≅ Z/l cuts out X̲_K, with l cusps ↔

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: F_l, and C̲_K = X̲_K/±1, with l± cusps ↔ |F_l|. Since j ∉ Z, E has no CM, so the K-core is C_F. For each p choose a v | p

text.font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'DejaVu Serif', 'FreeSerif', Inter, sans-serif

svg.text: in K; at a bad p, take the one where the line is the Tate subgroup μ_l. Finally ε̲ is the cusp ±1.
